html:
Tiburcio Carías Andino was a Honduran general and leader of the National Party, president and dictator of Honduras from 1933 to 1949.

He won the election of 1932, then stayed in power by rewriting the constitution and jailing or exiling opponents. He ruled through the army and the party, kept on good terms with the United Fruit Company, and was backed by the United States. The press was censored and many opponents were killed.

His years were a time of order and slow building of roads, with the airline TACA flying where roads did not go. Under pressure after the Second World War he stepped aside in 1949. He was one of a generation of Central American strongmen with Somoza in Nicaragua and Hernández Martínez in El Salvador, and his party remained a pillar of Honduras's politics.
sum: Tiburcio Carías Andino was a Honduran general and leader of the National Party, president and dictator of Honduras from 1933 to 1949.
